notes.okuzannya: Kucheza mpira, to play football; kucheza muziki, to dance.
notes.vyombo: Pots, plates and cups together. One: chombo.

guidebook.intro: Everyone helps at home. Learn the short commands you’ll hear every day, and how to ask for help politely.

tips.title: Commands: just the verb
body: To tell one person to do something, use the bare verb: **Leta!** (bring!), **Funga!** (close!), **Osha!** (wash!).
To several people, add **-ni**: **Fungeni mlango** (close the door, all of you). A few common ones are irregular: **Njoo** (come) becomes **Njooni**, and **Kaa** (sit) becomes **Kaeni**.

tips.title: Asking nicely: nisaidie
body: **Nisaidie** means “help me”. It is a softer form of the verb, ending in **-e**, that Swahili uses for wishes and polite requests: **ni-** (me) + **saidi(a)** + **-e**.
The same form gives “let’s”: **Tufanye kazi pamoja** (let’s work together), **Tusafishe** (let’s clean). With **tafadhali** it is always polite.

culture.title: Children help
body: From a young age, children fetch water, sweep the compound and wash dishes. Saying **Kazi nzuri!** or **Asante kwa msaada** to a child who helps is warmly received.
